```{=html}
<h3>About ANID and FONDECYT</h3>
<p>
  <strong>ANID</strong> (National Agency for Research and Development) is Chile's national
  research and innovation funding agency. It plays a role similar to the
  <em>National Science Foundation</em> (NSF) in the United States, <em>UKRI</em> in the United Kingdom,
  the <em>ANR</em> in France, the <em>DFG</em> in Germany or the <em>ARC</em> in Australia,
  and it is the Chilean counterpart of <em>CONICET</em> and <em>CNPq</em> as funders in Argentina and Brazil.
</p>
<p>
  <strong>FONDECYT</strong> (National Fund for Scientific and Technological Development) is ANID's main instrument for funding individual, investigator-driven basic research,
  awarded through national peer-reviewed competitions.
  <em>FONDECYT Regular</em> is comparable to an NSF standard research grant or a DFG Individual Research Grant,
  while <em>FONDECYT Initiation</em> targets early-career researchers, in the spirit of
  NSF CAREER or the ERC Starting Grant (at a smaller scale).
  These equivalences are approximate: budgets, durations and selection rules differ.
</p>
```
